title: Single dispatch authority on autonomous-intrusive runs — Claude becomes THE picker; next_best_action_selector and auto_queue_active are skipped or routed-through-Claude
goal: Today the autonomous-intrusive loop runs THREE competing dispatch engines in parallel: (1) auto_queue_active / auto_queue_passive rules in workers/orchestration that queue capability tasks based on signal triggers, (2) next_best_action_selector — a deterministic rule-based 'AI proposal' generator that wraps each pick in APPROVAL workflow, and (3) the Claude picker in assessment_loop.py. On run 3e2cfa5b all 14 AgentReasoning rows carried `next_best_action_selector_used=True` and `selector_decision='APPROVAL'` despite `autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True`. Claude was effectively advisory: 17 tasks dispatched mostly via auto-queue, Claude's picks repeatedly rejected (memory tool, empty exec_plan). #336 fixed the planner — this task fixes the dispatch layer. When `run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True`, the Claude picker is THE picker: auto_queue_active is skipped, next_best_action_selector emits suggestions for Claude to consume rather than directly creating APPROVAL proposals.
scope: Three coordinated edits across api/app/services + workers/orchestration: (1) `api/app/services/assessment_loop.py` — audit every `selector_decision='APPROVAL'` write-site (currently 2: lines ~2381 and ~3540). When `run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True`, replace APPROVAL with direct dispatch path. The selector's suggestions become inputs to the Claude picker prompt (existing `target_intel_plan` projection extends to include selector_top_3 candidates). (2) `workers/orchestration/tasks.py` — audit `_auto_queue_active_capabilities` / `_auto_queue_passive_capabilities` call sites. When `run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True`, skip auto-queue dispatch and emit a single AgentReasoning row 'auto-queue skipped (autonomous-intrusive mode); Claude picker is sole dispatch authority'. (3) `api/app/services/ai_agent.py` — `select_next_best_action_for_run` callers in this module also gate on `autonomous_intrusive_allowed`.
generation_reason: Empirical evidence from run 3e2cfa5b: 14/14 AgentReasoning rows have `next_best_action_selector_used=True` + `selector_decision='APPROVAL'` + `action_text='Create a reviewable AI proposal; execution waits for existing approval flow'`. The deterministic selector is treating an autonomous-intrusive run as if it were operator-supervised. Meanwhile auto_queue_active fired ~17 dispatches without Claude consultation. #336 fixed the planner-level bypass; this is the matching fix at the dispatch layer. Without this, the Claude picker can never be 'in charge' regardless of how good his reasoning gets.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Three coordinated edits at the documented sites only. Do NOT introduce a new flag — the existing `run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed` is the sole gate. Do NOT change non-autonomous run behavior (regression guard).
constraints.non_autonomous_path_preserved: For runs with autonomous_intrusive_allowed=False (operator-supervised default), behavior is UNCHANGED: APPROVAL wrappers fire, auto_queue runs, selector emits proposals. The bypass strictly opens autonomous behavior, never closes operator-supervised behavior.
constraints.approval_path_still_exists: The approval workflow code path stays intact for the non-autonomous case. We are NOT removing approvals; we are skipping them only when the operator explicitly opted into autonomous-intrusive.

success_criteria: All `selector_decision='APPROVAL'` write sites in assessment_loop.py + ai_agent.py are gated on `not run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed`. When the flag is True, the code path takes direct dispatch instead.

auto_queue_active / auto_queue_passive in workers/orchestration/tasks.py gate on `not run.autonomous_intrusive_allowed`. When True, auto-queue is skipped + a single audit AgentReasoning row records the skip.

When auto_queue is skipped, the next_best_action_selector's top-3 candidates are projected into the picker prompt (new helper `_collect_selector_suggestions(run, scope) -> list[dict]` reuses select_next_best_action_for_run internally) so Claude has the deterministic candidates as INPUT, not COMPETITION.

Live re-test on backlog-406 harness: on ≥1 of the 5 targets with autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True, 0 AgentReasoning rows have selector_decision='APPROVAL'. ≥80% of dispatched tasks have `decision_source='ai_loop_claude_picker'`.
Live re-test on a 2nd target: same metrics.
Regression: a non-autonomous run still produces APPROVAL-wrapped proposals + auto_queue dispatches. Verifiable via DB query on a control run.

Unit tests: (a) flag=False preserves all 3 dispatch paths; (b) flag=True skips auto_queue + replaces APPROVAL with direct dispatch + threads selector suggestions to picker; (c) source-grep sentinel asserts the gate is consistently applied at every write site (test fails if a future refactor introduces a new APPROVAL write site without the gate).
must_not_touch: approvals.py / approval_workflows.py — the approval flow code stays intact, only its CALLERS gate on the new condition
api/app/models/control.py (no schema changes; the existing autonomous_intrusive_allowed column is the sole input)
workers/runners/ — runners are agnostic to which dispatcher fired them
ui-v2/ — UI continues to display whatever dispatch records get written

acceptance_criteria: Live test on ≥2 unrelated real-world targets (per feedback_live_proof_must_be_diverse_real_targets) with autonomous_intrusive_allowed=True: 0 AgentReasoning rows have selector_decision='APPROVAL'. Claude picker is dispatch authority.
Live test on a non-autonomous control run on one of the same targets: APPROVAL workflow still fires (regression check).
Source-grep sentinel: all selector_decision='APPROVAL' write sites are gated on the flag.
